correctness.rationale: The two-state Feynman–Kac clock transform has factor f_gamma solving f''+2 gamma f'-(lambda h)^2 f=0 with f(0)=1,f'(0)=0. Its time derivative is positive for t>0; differentiation in gamma gives a forced ODE with strictly negative source -2f' and positive Green kernel, hence partial_gamma f<0. For uniform initial spatial position, Dirichlet–Neumann heat content is the positive-weight sum |integral phi_j|^2/|Omega| times positive clock modes, with positive ground-state weight; this gives strict first-order absorption-time stochastic ordering for each t>0 and bounded connected regular domain. On a fully absorbing interval, subtracting state-averaged coupled backward equations gives the scalar positive Dirichlet resolvent and the exact hyperbolic-cosine mean formula, strictly decreasing at fixed interior x. Frozen gamma=0 and homogenized gamma->infinity limits match; no claim of full stochastic order from a fixed nonuniform start. Source checks use direct formula algebra, not finite-difference tests as universal proof.
